page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the ARMv9 AWS Graviton architecture. The instance provides 192 dedicated physical cores across 192 vCPUs using Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.7 GHz, with no simultaneous multithreading. It features 384.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), 11,400 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. It contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark data reflects high-density parallel compute capabilities alongside modest single-core throughput. While single-thread tests such as stress-ng single-core (1,643.88) and Geekbench single-core (1,656.0) perform in the middle 50%, multi-threaded metrics place within the top tier. Notable results include a stress-ng multi-core score of 311,373.11, a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 1,367.53 GB/sec, and a Geekbench clang compilation score of 86,720.0. Memory subsystems also demonstrate high throughput, reaching 907.71 GB/sec on large uncached read operations and 402.56 GB/sec on writes.

Data serving benchmarks show exceptional throughput, evidenced by 362.69 million Redis SET operations per second, static web serving throughput of 169.75 GB/sec, and a top-tier PassMark database operations score of 46,609.13. However, small-model LLM prompt processing registers in the bottom 25% (285.67 tokens/sec), reflecting the absence of discrete matrix acceleration or specialized GPU hardware.

The 2:1 vCPU-to-memory ratio, coupled with 11.4 TB of high-speed local NVMe storage and high core density, provides efficient resource utilization for horizontal scaling without paying for excess RAM. Tradeoffs involve ARM architecture compatibility requirements and single-thread execution limits compared to higher-frequency x86 processors. Best-fit workloads include large-scale software compilation, distributed caching, high-concurrency web serving, batch compression, and I/O-intensive database clusters.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.48xlarge is an ARM-based compute-optimized instance powered by 192 dedicated Neoverse-V2 cores running at 2.7 GHz on the AWS Nitro System. Configured with a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, it supplies 384.0 GB of RAM alongside 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 50 Gbps baseline networking, without discrete GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded compute, memory bandwidth, and I/O serving capabilities, demonstrated by 362.69 million Redis SET operations per second and a multi-core stress-ng score of 311,373.11, contrasted against average single-core performance. The combination of dense physical core counts, high uncached memory throughput, and massive integrated NVMe storage makes c8gd.48xlarge an efficient platform for massive distributed workloads, including software compilation pipelines, in-memory caches, high-throughput static web serving, and high-concurrency database deployments.
